decisions.reason: Having remained in the portfolio after launch, this turnaround management software fits the firm's strategy of integrated, data-driven airport operations and is likely to be retained.
The apron connectivity module strengthens the firm's broader airport software stack and installed-base integration, so continued market presence is more likely than withdrawal.
Revenue calculation and billing is somewhat less central than safety and operational control products, but it still supports the firm's end-to-end airport platform and service model.
Apron equipment monitoring is closely tied to the firm's maintenance, lifecycle service, and analytics capabilities, which makes keeping it the more plausible choice.
Apron resource management directly supports throughput and bottleneck reduction at airports, aligning well with the firm's core value proposition.
A controller safety alert service is highly consistent with the firm's safety-focused tower and airside portfolio, so taking it off the market soon appears unlikely.
